I hope that helps.

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject_clean: [poppr] Poppr amova issue with subsetting variance among pop, among samples within pop, and within sample
messages.body_plain:
Hello Alexis,

This is a bit odd indeed. The default of poppr.amova() is to automatically calculate within-individual variance. I suspect it has something to do with the fact that vcfR only exports its alleles as zeroes and ones. Would you be willing to (privately) send me a copy of your data so that I can try to reproduce this?

In the meantime, one other thing you might try if you have a compiler on your computer is to use the development version of vcfR (remotes::install_github("knausb/vcfR")) and use vcfR2genind(vcf, return.alleles = TRUE).

Let me know if that helps.

Best,
Zhian

I failed to find this information in the latest manual / online Intro. Any pointers are highly appreciated, as I'm setting up a chain of major studies (up to 1,200 Inds).

Thanks in advance!
-M

Hello M,

What your colleague might be referring to is the genotype accumulation curve: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/genotype_curve.html

This curve is primarily useful for clonal data sets and can tell you if you have selected enough loci to resolve all of the unique multilocus genotypes in your sample. Arnaud-Haond et al 2007 describe its use well, IMO
https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-294X.2007.03535.x
